---
title: "Decision sheet"
description: "A one-page decision sheet that turns the model passport into a recommendation with conditions, responsibilities and a review date, with guidance and example entries for the fracture-alert case."
---

The model passport describes what the model can do. The decision sheet states what should happen now, for whom,
under which conditions and who is responsible. Keep the two documents separate: a good model can still lead to the
recommendation "not yet", and a modest model can be worth piloting under clear conditions.

## Template

| Section | Your entry | Guidance and example entry (fracture alert, fictitious) |
|---|---|---|
| **Decision** | | One sentence that someone can act on. *"Pilot the alert in shadow mode for three months; do not show it to clinicians yet."* |
| **People affected** | | Who gains, who carries the errors, who has to do extra work. *Older patients with subtle signs; ED clinicians; radiology.* |
| **Options considered** | | Including doing nothing. *Usual care; alert shown to clinicians; shadow mode only.* |
| **Recommendation and conditions** | | What must hold for the recommendation to stand. *Local sensitivity in people aged 75 and older measured on at least the number of fractures agreed in advance.* |
| **Counter-position** | | The strongest argument against, stated fairly. *"Shadow mode delays any benefit for patients by months."* |
| **Ethics** | | The conflict of goals and how it is resolved; how patients are informed. |
| **Regulation** | | Intended purpose, role (manufacturer, deployer), relevant source, classification status (*open* if not confirmed), missing document. |
| **Data protection** | | Data flow with purpose, legal basis question, recipients, deletion point; DPIA pre-check. |
| **Information security** | | One threat, its control, the test that shows it works, the responsible role. |
| **Responsibility** | | Who decides, who monitors, who can switch the tool off. Functional roles, not names. |
| **Stop or override condition** | | A measurable trigger. *"Switch off if the weekly false-alert rate exceeds the agreed limit, or if an unapproved model version is detected."* |
| **Next review date** | | A date and what will be reviewed then. |
| **Open points** | | Each with the information that would close it and the responsible role. |

## Checks before you hand it in

- Can someone who has not seen your presentation act on the first line?
- Is every number on the sheet also in the model passport, with its denominator?
- Are ethics, regulation, data protection and security each addressed with a fact from your case, not with a
  general statement?
- Does the sheet say who can stop the tool, and on which observation?

- [B27 · Model passport, study report and decision](https://cttir.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b27-model-passport-study-report.html#sec-b27-core).
- [B20 · Pilot operation, impact and monitoring](https://cttir.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b20-pilot-operation-monitoring.html#sec-b20-core)
  – shadow mode, monitoring and stop criteria.
- [B21 · Ethics at the bedside and in study design](https://cttir.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b21-ethics.html#sec-b21-core)
  – conflicts of goals and the perspective of people affected.
